chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, who said:
I asked Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about drinking the fermented drink, so he abhorred it with an intense abhorrence.

key_terms.الْفُقَّاعِ: A specific type of fermented drink, often identified as barley wine or a similar beverage in classical sources.
key_terms.كَرَاهَةً شَدِيدَةً: Intense abhorrence/dislike, emphasizing the strength of the ruling.
key_terms.كَرِهَهُ: He disliked it; a technical term in fiqh indicating a status between permissible and forbidden, often translated as makruh.

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on drinking fuqqa' according to Imam Al-Hasan (as)?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) expresses strong aversion (*karahat shadidah*) to drinking *al-fuqqa*, a specific type of fermented beverage, highlighting the nuanced Shia approach to intoxicants that may not be strictly prohibited but are discouraged for purity. This ruling reflects the broader jurisprudential distinction between *khamr* (intoxicant) and other fermented drinks, emphasizing spiritual and physical cleanliness. The strong dislike serves as a practical guideline for believers to avoid potential impurities associated with fermentation processes.
